answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by binding each identity to a costly, verifiable reputation ledger: before an agent can join, it must stake resources and build an atlas of attested interactions — every trade, review, and handshake recorded and signed. New identities start with only a faint pulse of trust that grows through real work, while a plume of fake accounts launched at once stands out because none of them carry history. Forging a past costs more than the attack gains.
